    Meet Lina Zaghloul, a Digital Solutions Manager at ENGIE Solutions Middle East with over a decade of experience across banking, energy, and the FM industry. With a background in industrial engineering and a Master’s degree in Data Science, Lina leverages her technical expertise to develop innovative, practical solutions that enhance operational efficiency.

    Lina credits much of her success and drive to her brother, Bilal, who has been her biggest mentor and source of inspiration. From an early age, Bilal’s guidance and work ethic shaped her professional outlook, encouraging her to aim high and approach challenges with confidence and resilience. His unwavering support and insight have played a pivotal role in shaping her career and the person she has become today.

    Her advice: “Don’t wait for recognition—be proactive in highlighting your achievements and advocating for your own growth. Embrace failure as a learning experience, and maintain your curiosity by seeking new knowledge and experiences.”

    Read her story here: https://lnkd.in/g7M2egDD

    What are the odds that my first issue as editor of Facilities Management Middle East celebrates the women redefining FM? If you ask me, it feels just right. The March issue of FM Middle East is out! https://lnkd.in/d7p5nNW3

    The industry has long been considered male-dominated, but working on this issue made one thing abundantly clear: women are not just part of the conversation; they are leading it. They’re heading teams, making bold decisions, and proving every day that FM is a field for those with the vision and drive to push it forward. This issue hands the mic to a few of the many women making an impact in FM, and trust me, their insights, experiences, and advice are worth every bit of attention. Featured in the list: Andrea Yoko, fatema yusuf fakhruddin, Karla Reid, Nadia Ibrahim, Sam Emery, SABIHA ABDULLAH, Lara Paemen, Rekha Harikumar, Sangeetha, Lina Zaghloul, Kamini Raghunathan, and Aishwarya Ranjith

    Our cover story takes a closer look at how Ejadah is setting new benchmarks by integrating technology, sustainability, and client-focused strategies to transform facilities management. We spoke with Sijo Elias, Assistant Director – Client Relations at Ejadah, about the company’s approach to innovation and how it’s shaping the future of FM.

    We also caught up with Irene Vidal, CEO of Facilities Maintenance Management, LLC. (FMM), who shared her insights on how Qatar’s FM sector is evolving and what’s driving these changes.

    The issue also explores how technology is bridging the sector’s skills gap, Javeria Aijaz's take on the trends shaping Saudi Arabia’s FM industry in 2025, and more.

    Today’s Idea: thanks Lina Zaghloul

    Nature vs. Nurture: What Shapes Us More?

    Are we born with our abilities, personality, and intelligence, or do we develop them through experience? The age-old nature vs. nurture debate reminds us that human traits emerge from both.
     • Nature gives us genetic predispositions—our biological blueprint. Think of eye color, height, or even some personality tendencies.
     • Nurture shapes us through life experiences—our upbringing, education, and social environment refine who we become.

    Some traits are hardwired, like reflexes or natural talents, while others evolve with effort, exposure, and learning. Intelligence, for instance, has a genetic foundation but thrives with curiosity, discipline, and the right environment.

    The truth? It’s never just one or the other. Our potential is born, but growth is built. Nature sets the stage, nurture directs the play.
